_law: EVERY NEW FIGHT VISUAL ARRIVES WITH ITS COST (VAMILY [draw budget], COMBAT lane, 9/7/26). Anything new that draws inside the fight is designed and built, but it ships with its cost stated in MILLISECONDS PER BEAT and does not enter the fight loop until there is room for it. Not an art freeze and not a stop: one rule, a number with every new thing that draws.
_how: Numbers are taken by tools/bohemia_draw_cost.js, never typed. It pins the camera, interleaves the feature on and off frame by frame, calls the fight's own draw() and reports the median difference. Held by gates/draw_budget_gate.js.
_unit: ms_per_beat = ms_per_draw x 30. A beat at 120 BPM is 500 ms and the fight draws one frame per animation frame; 30 is 60 fps, an upper bound stated on purpose, because the measured fight runs 41-56.
driven_beat_source: records/BOHEMIA_A_FIGHT_NOBODY_IS_PLAYING_9_7_26.md, PLUMBER lane 9/7: seven driven samples, median 413.5, worst 497.5, best 347. THE HEADROOM IS NOT A NUMBER, IT IS A RANGE, and which end you get is decided by whether the camera happens to be still.

features.name: NOTHING (the noise floor)
features.what: the same setting in both arms, so the number this reports is what this instrument reads when there is nothing to read. Any feature whose cost is not clearly above this line is BELOW THE FLOOR, and the honest answer is 'too small for this instrument', never zero.

features.name: the companion on the field
features.what: a second body, her ring, her name and her health bar, drawn with the same human art every fighter uses

features.name: the beat ghost
features.what: the teaching fight's one man fades out between beats, so a stranger can SEE that he is only there on the beat
features.toggle_note: THE COMPANION IS HELD OFF IN BOTH ARMS ON PURPOSE. The first toggle was G.teachBeat alone and it measured the ghost at MINUS one millisecond a beat, outside its own error bar. allyOn() reads teachBeat too -- the teaching fight is yours alone -- so switching the ghost on was also removing a whole second body from the frame, and the tool was reporting the companion's cost with the sign flipped. A toggle that moves two things measures neither.
features.in_loop_note: the first fight only, and it turns itself off for good once that fight is won

features.name: the way out marker
features.what: the pulsing blue disc, dashed ring and OUT label on the tile that ends the fight
features.note: not this lane's row, and it is in here as a CALIBRATION: a feature everybody agrees is cheap and visible, so a run of the tool that reports nothing for it is the tool being broken rather than the feature being free.

features.name: the camera pull-back and the cloud shadow
features.row: V205 [enter zoom] HOW-THE-FIGHT-BEGINS, ruled by Paolo 9/6, look card DIRECTION 9/6, SHIPPED 9/11
features.what: the view zooms out from person-scale to house-scale over the same ground across TWO BEATS, with a cloud shadow (a value multiplier, 0.78 at its core) travelling across the frame over the moment the scale changes
features.note: SHIPPED, AND IT COSTS THE FIGHT LOOP ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION, which is why this row could ship against 2.5 ms of worst-case headroom. Nothing new draws inside the fight: the pull-back and the shade are the CITY's and the cover over the swap is the SHELL's, all of it during a HANDOVER, which is not the fight loop. The draw-surface ratchet is the proof: the combat blob is unchanged at 15 functions. MEASURED IN THE CITY, per call, on the real surface: the shade 0.1 ms, one paint of the pull-back 0.1 ms, the photograph (including its one blurred copy for the surround) 3 ms once, and the live render it sits on top of during beat one 2-3 ms, which is the render the city was already doing. AND THE THING THAT DOMINATES ALL OF THEM IS NOT OURS: this machine stalls the walked city for up to 1475 ms with nothing running at all (measured, 10 fps baseline), which is why the handover is on a clock and not on a frame count.
features._zero_note: THERE IS NO PER-DRAW NUMBER FOR THIS ROW AND THAT IS THE POINT: it never draws inside the fight, so there is nothing for the instrument to put a stopwatch on. A row that carried a measured-looking 0.0 here would be claiming the tool read zero, which it never did. The floor flag is about the INSTRUMENT's resolution and says nothing about a feature that is not in the loop at all, so the gate holds this row to a different test: zero by construction is only allowed with in_loop false and a reason written down.

_ratchet: THE FIGHT'S DRAW SURFACE, ratcheted. Every function in the blob whose name begins with draw is listed here. A lane that adds one is adding a new thing that draws, and the rule says it arrives with its cost -- so the gate goes red until the name is in this list AND the ledger carries a priced row for it. This is the half of the rule that cannot be talked around: a declaration nobody has to make is not a rule.
_total_note: The sum of every priced feature that is IN the loop today. It is stored so a change to it has to be written down, and recomputed by the gate so it cannot drift from the rows.
